status_summary: Executive Order 14183 (signed 2025-01-27) directed DOD to bar military service by people whose gender identity differs from their birth sex. A Hegseth memo of 2025-02-07 paused new accessions of people with a history of gender dysphoria and paused transition-related medical procedures, and a policy of 2025-02-26 disqualifies applicants and current members with a current or past diagnosis or a history of medical or surgical transition, ends transition-related medical care and requires administrative separation (as described in the D.C. Circuit's opinion); a May 2025 directive started voluntary, then involuntary, separations. An Associated Press figure cited by Military Times puts the number of service members with a gender dysphoria diagnosis at about 4,240. The Supreme Court stayed the Shilling injunction on 2025-05-06 (No. 24A1030), so enforcement proceeded. On 2026-06-01 the D.C. Circuit (No. 25-5087), in a divided decision, affirmed the Talbott preliminary injunction in part as to the named plaintiffs who are currently serving, vacated it as to named plaintiffs seeking to enlist, and narrowed it to the named plaintiffs; a class was certified on 2026-06-30 (the injunction has not been reported as extended to the class). On 2026-08-27 the Solicitor General filed a petition for certiorari (United States v. Talbott, No. 26-272); respondents' brief in opposition was submitted on 2026-11-02, and the docket shows no distribution for conference and no ruling, and a trial is reported as set for January 2027.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14183 signed. It directs DOD to set standards that exclude people whose gender identity differs from their birth sex and to update medical standards for entry and retention.

Secretary Hegseth issues Additional Guidance on Prioritizing Military Excellence and Readiness (following a 2025-02-07 memo that paused new accessions and transition-related medical procedures). As described in the D.C. Circuit's opinion, it disqualifies applicants and current members with a current or past gender dysphoria diagnosis or a history of medical or surgical transition, ends transition-related medical and surgical treatment, and requires administrative separation of disqualified members, with narrow waivers.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (opinion, No. 25-5087)

timeline.event: Judge Ana Reyes (D.D.C.) issues a universal preliminary injunction against the Hegseth policy in Talbott v. United States (775 F. Supp. 3d 283), finding the plaintiffs likely to succeed on an equal protection claim as the D.C. Circuit later describes it; the court denies a motion to dissolve it on 2025-03-26. The government appeals.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (opinion, No. 25-5087)

timeline.event: The Supreme Court grants the government's application in United States v. Shilling (No. 24A1030) and stays the W.D. Wash. preliminary injunction of 2025-03-27 pending disposition of the Ninth Circuit appeal and any certiorari petition; Justices Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson would have denied the application. DOD may resume separations while appeals continue.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States (docket No. 24A1030)

timeline.event: Hegseth memo orders separations: self-identification deadlines of June 6 (active duty) and July 7 (Guard and Reserve), with involuntary separation to follow. Reporting at the time said about 1,000 had self-identified.

The D.C. Circuit (Wilkins, Walker and Rogers, JJ.; No. 25-5087; argued 2026-01-22) affirms the Talbott preliminary injunction in part and vacates it in part: it stands for the named plaintiffs who are currently serving, is vacated for named plaintiffs seeking to enlist, and is narrowed to the named plaintiffs. Judge Wilkins announces the judgment, Judge Rogers concurs in part and dissents in part, and Judge Walker dissents; press reports describe the decision as 2-1.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (opinion, No. 25-5087)

timeline.event: The district court (Judge Reyes) certifies Talbott as a class action of service members challenging the policy; Law360 reports that the judge raised concerns about whether proposed class counsel can adequately represent the class. The report does not give the class definition or say whether the injunction reaches the class.

The Solicitor General files a petition for a writ of certiorari in United States v. Talbott (No. 26-272) seeking review of the D.C. Circuit's 2026-06-01 decision; the case is docketed 2026-09-01. Respondents' time to respond is extended to 2026-11-02 (order of 2026-09-25), amicus briefs supporting the government were filed 2026-10-01, and respondents' brief in opposition is entered as submitted on 2026-11-02. The docket shows no distribution for conference and no ruling. Stars and Stripes reports that a two-week trial is set for January 2027.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States (docket No. 26-272)
